spec: dispatch://LEGION-88/spec (version 2; Requirements, Design, Errors, Testing are binding)
goal: Prove the daemon's existing pane-environment allow-list from a worker pane, make the smoke rig fail when a pane carries a Legion identity the daemon did not set or the controller never claimed its role, and make the two remaining silences speak: the daemon logs when it retires a live-but-unregistered controller or root, and the extension says why it refused a pane with both launch markers instead of throwing into the host.
architecture: Four independent slices in one pull request. (1) Extension: classify.ts throws a typed ConflictingLaunchMarkersError for the both-markers case (message unchanged); legion.ts catches exactly that error in session_start (announce once on the pane, continue as not-legion, never exit) and in tool_call (first-call classification becomes 'not a phase worker' instead of rethrowing every call). (2) Daemon: a runtime-neutral describeProcessLocation(locator) helper in runtime.ts (beside locatorHandles/sameProcess, so ProcessManager still never reads a runtime-specific locator field), a registrationDeadlineMs getter shared by both arm sites, and one console.error line before the stop in retireAndRespawnStuckController and in retireUnconfirmedRoot's alive branch. (3) Rig: checkpoint 14 in scripts/smoke/checkpoints.sh, ungated by SMOKE_WEBHOOK_MODE, requiring the controller role claim in state.json and checking every recorded pane's process tree against the identity the daemon recorded for it plus the private server's global table; checkpoints.test.sh gains a per-pane pid map in its fake tmux and four cases; README/up.sh/up.test.sh gating text names 14. (4) Docs: the config-env-keys solution doc, daemon AGENTS.md, pi-envoy AGENTS.md. Then the rig proof (positive from the implementer's own pane with nothing unset; negative in none mode with SMOKE_OMP_LAUNCH_PREFIX prefixed by `env LEGION_TREE=CANARY-1` and a short LEGION_WORKER_BOOT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS).
groundTruthsVerified: GT1 (no new scrub anywhere): packages/daemon/src/daemon/environment.ts:103 PANE_ENV_ALLOW_LIST names no LEGION_* variable (its doc comment at :99-102 says LEGION_*/DISPATCH_* are explicit per-pane -e pairs, never inherited); paneEnvironment (:198) lays mise env over the allow-listed subset and drops credential-shaped names. scripts/smoke/up.sh has no env -u for the identity family (its only `env -u` is GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN inside the App-token helper at :358-360) and no preflight for LEGION_*. Nothing about the scrub changes in this plan; up.sh's only edit is one word in its none-mode block-reason string (checkpoint 14 joins 8 and 13 as ungated).

GT2 (extension throw escapes): packages/pi-envoy/extensions/legion.ts:725 `const classification = classifySession(process.env);` inside pi.on("session_start") with no try/catch, so classify.ts:12's `throw new Error("Legion session has both controller and tree launch markers")` escapes to the host. legion.ts:761 `phaseWorkerPane ??= classifySession(process.env).kind === "phase-worker";` in the tool_call hook: a throw leaves phaseWorkerPane undefined, so the same throw recurs on every tool call.

GT3 (silent retirements): packages/daemon/src/daemon/processes.ts retireAndRespawnStuckController (:2356-2378) reaches stopProcess at :2368 with no log line on the success path (only the failure catch at :2370 logs); retireUnconfirmedRoot's alive branch (:2320-2338) reaches stopProcessSerialized at :2324 with no log line (only the failure catch at :2326 logs). Both waits are armed for workerBootTimeoutSeconds * 1000 * workerBootRegistrationDeadlineIntervals (duplicated at :1972-1975 and :2004-2007; defaults 120 * 3 = 360 s, config.ts:183-184). processes.ts uses console.error for all 48 `[legion]` lines and never console.warn.

GT4 (state shape and rig mapping): scripts/smoke/checkpoints.sh reads the raw persisted LegionState at ${SMOKE_DIR}/daemon/state.json via state() (:28-31), not the redacted HTTP endpoint. The controller role claim is state.roles["legion-<project>-controller"] (controllerToken, packages/contracts/src/legion-roles.ts:66-69; project is the slug, e.g. legion-exampleorg24-controller for SMOKE_PROJECT=example-org/24 — checkpoints.sh's project_slug() computes it): an object with role "controller" and sessionId and no `issue` field, which is why checkpoint 13's `.roles[]? | select(has("issue"))` excludes it. Checkpoint 1 (:checkpoint_one) checks only .controllerLocator's window/pane and never the claim. A root pane is trees[KEY].locator (tmuxWindowId/tmuxPaneId/panePid...) and the daemon sets LEGION_TREE=LEGION_ISSUE=KEY on it (processes.ts:2875-2876); a worker pane is roles[token].locator with roles[token].issue, and the daemon sets LEGION_TREE=<tree key> LEGION_ISSUE=<claim issue> (processes.ts:3188-3189; a sub-architect on a child has LEGION_TREE the root and LEGION_ISSUE the child). The controller pane gets LEGION_CONTROLLER=1, LEGION_ROLE=controller, LEGION_DAEMON_URL, LEGION_PROJECT, the credential env, and LEGION_CONTROLLER_SECRET_FILE — none of LEGION_TREE/LEGION_ISSUE/LEGION_GENERATION/LEGION_WORKSPACE (processes.ts:3360-3366; processes.test.ts:903-909 asserts the exact set). Checkpoint 13 (:671-713) resolves each recorded pane id to its pid with `legion_tmux display-message -p -t <pane> '#{pane_pid}'`, reads names from /proc/<pid>/environ via `tr '\0' '\n' | grep -m1 "^NAME="`, fails `cannot read /proc/<pid>` when unreadable, and reads the private server's global table with `legion_tmux show-environment -g`.

GT5 (why the checkpoint must walk descendants): every pane runs `cd && worker-shim --socket

-- ` (runtime-tmux.ts:288) and withOmpLaunchPrefix puts omp_launch_prefix at the front of innerCommand, so `env LEGION_TREE=CANARY-1 ...` executes below worker-shim: the injected identity is on the OMP process and its children, not on the pane's own pid. A checkpoint that read only the pane pid would pass the negative rig. Checkpoint 14 therefore inspects each recorded pane's pid and every descendant.

GT6 (rig knobs): up.sh's generated legion.yaml sets no worker_boot_timeout_seconds key and its `start_process daemon env ...` passes the ambient environment through, so an exported LEGION_WORKER_BOOT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS reaches the rig daemon (config.ts:1117-1123 reads it when the file omits the key). SMOKE_OMP_LAUNCH_PREFIX is whitespace-split into the omp_launch_prefix YAML list (up.sh:363-381), so `env LEGION_TREE=CANARY-1 secrets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY GEMINI_API_KEY OPENAI_API_KEY --` is valid. The rig daemon log is ${SMOKE_DIR}/daemon.log; RIG READY prints before the controller has claimed (spec rejected waiting there).

GT7 (which error the canary rig raises): the daemon sets LEGION_ROLE=controller on the controller pane (processes.ts:3361); classifySession checks the LEGION_CONTROLLER + LEGION_TREE pair first (classify.ts:11-13) before it reads LEGION_ROLE, so on the canary rig the error raised is exactly the both-markers one the extension catch targets, never the isLegionRole refusal.

produces: checkpoint_fourteen semantics. Inputs: state() (raw state.json), legion_tmux, project_slug. Checks, in order: (a) `.roles["legion-<slug>-controller"]` is an object with `.role == "controller"` and a non-empty `.sessionId`, else `fail "daemon state has no controller role claim (legion-<slug>-controller): the controller pane never registered — attach with \`tmux -L legion-<slug> attach -t legion-<slug>\` and read its pane"`. (b) Build the pane list with expectations from state via one jq program: controller → `{pane: .controllerLocator.tmuxPaneId, kind: "controller"}`; each `trees[KEY].locator.tmuxPaneId` → `{kind: "root", tree: KEY, issue: KEY}`; each `roles[token]` with an `issue` and a `locator.tmuxPaneId` → `{kind: "worker", token, issue, tree: tree_of(issue)}` where `tree_of(k)` is k when `.trees[k]` exists, else `tree_of(.issues[k].parent)` when a parent is recorded, else k (jq: `. as $s | def tree_of(k): if $s.trees[k] then k elif $s.issues[k].parent then tree_of($s.issues[k].parent) else k end; ...`) — mirrors liveAncestorTree: a sub-architect on a child has LEGION_TREE the root and LEGION_ISSUE the child; a root architect claim (issue == tree) yields the same expectation as its tree entry, so a pane listed twice is checked twice with identical expectations (harmless; dedupe by pane id in bash if preferred). Skip entries whose pane id is null. Require at least one pane (the controller's), else fail like 13. (c) For each pane: `pid=$(legion_tmux display-message -p -t "$pane" '#{pane_pid}')` or fail `recorded pane <pane> is absent from <socket>`; `[[ -r /proc/$pid/environ ]]` or fail `cannot read /proc/<pid>` (as 13); collect `descendant_pids <pid>` — one `ps -eo pid=,ppid=` snapshot, breadth-first from the pane pid, inclusive — and for each pid: if `/proc/<pid>` no longer exists skip it (a child that exited between snapshot and read), else if environ is unreadable fail naming the pid, else read `tr '\0' '\n' </proc/<pid>/environ`. Controller kind: any of LEGION_TREE, LEGION_ISSUE, LEGION_GENERATION, LEGION_WORKSPACE present → `fail "controller pane <pane> (pid <pid>) carries <NAME>: a Legion identity the daemon did not set for it — the rig launcher inherited it from an outer Legion pane, or the launch prefix injected it"`. Root/worker kind: LEGION_TREE present and != expected tree → `fail "pane <pane> (pid <pid>, <kind> <issue>) carries a LEGION_TREE that differs from the tree the daemon recorded for it (<tree>)"`; LEGION_ISSUE present and != expected issue → the same for LEGION_ISSUE. Absence never fails a root/worker pane: a worker's own subprocess may legitimately run under `env -u LEGION_TREE ...` (docs/solutions/legion/worker-pane-shell-gotchas.md), and the pane pid always carries both from its -e pairs anyway. Observed values are never printed; the recorded key is. (d) `legion_tmux show-environment -g | grep -m1 -E '^LEGION_[A-Za-z0-9_]*='` → `fail "private tmux server global environment names <NAME>"` (the `-NAME` unset markers do not match the anchor).
